entries.title: De Groote Keijser, the squat that became a fortress
entries.reason: private housing, no plaque
entries.hook: Squatters turned six canal houses into a fortress in 1978; the mayor refused to send the police.

entries.title: The gaper of Het Heertje, now "O Johnny"
entries.reason: sensitive: tell it factually
entries.hook: A stolen drugstore gaper, a replica removed in a 2020 racism row, then a two-faced Medusa gaper.

entries.title: Reestraat 6, Anton de Kom's Amsterdam house
entries.reason: dates of his stay differ; plaque unconfirmed
entries.hook: The anti-colonial writer of "Wij slaven van Suriname" lived here in 1935; Stadsherstel saved the near-ruin.

entries.title: Brouwersgracht stones: a bag of coins and a cowherd who stayed home
entries.hook: A money bag that "won't give to friends", dated 1772, and other stones Stadsherstel rescued.

entries.title: De Poezenboot
entries.reason: second tier (Atlas Obscura)
entries.hook: A woman took in one cat and kittens in 1966; now a purpose-built ark, still a working shelter.

entries.title: Descartes at Westermarkt 6
entries.reason: beside A-list Westerkerk; second source to find
entries.hook: Descartes lived here in 1634 and fathered a daughter with the housekeeper; a pavement tile says "Ik denk, dus ik ben".

entries.title: Zuid-Afrikahuis and the "boekverdrinking"
entries.reason: say "since 1950" for the library
entries.hook: Europe's largest library on South Africa, where masked activists threw books into the canal in 1984.

entries.title: The Heerenlogement gate on the Keizersgracht
entries.reason: lions are 1975 renewals
entries.hook: The gate of "the noblest taverne in the world" was carried here by its last auctioneer when the inn fell in 1874.

entries.title: The Knobbeliep: Amsterdam's own knobbly elms, Westermarkt and Nieuwe Herengracht
entries.reason: two pins in two zones
entries.hook: An undescribed elm cultivar with a burred trunk; only five are known, one an 1891 veteran on the Nieuwe Herengracht.

entries.title: The thickest tree in Centrum, a plane at Molenpad 2
entries.reason: or a Look for in the Molenpad draft (gg-west-3)
entries.hook: An oriental plane 5.75 m round, planted for a bank around 1860.

entries.title: Bergstraat: De Naaister and the corn measurer who came home
entries.reason: no second source; statue's house number and date unclear
entries.hook: Residents' own bronze seamstress, and a 1608 gable stone found in another building's hall and brought back.

entries.title: Klipper Bestevaer at the head of the Keizersgracht
entries.reason: single source; private boat
entries.hook: A 1906 clipper lived in as a home; a storm-felled elm snapped both masts in 2023, neighbours rallied.

entries.title: De Notendop, the Tuesday duet with the Westertoren
entries.reason: Still there? (not known to have resumed after the tower's restoration)
entries.hook: A home-built music tub answers the carillon on trumpet; the carillonneur waves through a hatch in the clock.

entries.title: Hildo Krop's comic strip on the telephone exchange, Herengracht 295
entries.reason: Okay; panels' subject unknown, no second source
entries.hook: The city sculptor's 1957 relief on the PTD exchange, which the register says reads like a comic strip.

entries.title: Nine Streets, stones saved from demolitions
entries.reason: Okay; scout suggests a Look for line instead
entries.hook: Stones saved from houses pulled down in 1950, and the Oranjeappel orphanage gate.

entries.title: The garden house that travelled, Keizersgracht 62-64
entries.reason: Okay; not visible from the street
entries.hook: A 1699 garden house, dismantled in 1917, found overgrown in 1966 and rebuilt behind another canal house.

entries.title: Pottenbakkersgang, a path older than the canal belt
entries.reason: Okay; single source; nothing marked
entries.hook: A pre-1612 path absorbed into the canal belt, still traceable between Herengracht 151 and 155.

entries.title: Langestraat 80, the Tsar in the gable and the Hollandsche Mediaeval
entries.reason: Okay; single source; next to "The tailors' saint" (no. 78)
entries.hook: Studio of the type designer of the Hollandsche Mediaeval; Stadsherstel's second restoration.

entries.title: The Fault in Our Stars bench, Leidsegracht
entries.reason: Okay; fan spot, thin on history
entries.hook: A film bench where young readers come to cry; stolen, replaced, still visited.

entries.title: Herenstraat 21, Meijer and Regina Turfkruier
entries.reason: Okay; single source
entries.hook: Shopkeepers researched their house and had stumbling stones laid in 2026; inside, Regina's ring and purse.

entries.title: Waterline, the red climber on the Leliegracht quay
entries.reason: Okay; probably temporary; spot to fix on site
entries.hook: An unannounced red figure paints a waterline high on the quay wall, a climate warning since 2025.

entries.title: De Afstap, the wool shop that kept its name
entries.reason: Okay; single source; shop; number not printed
entries.hook: Fifty years of wool; knitted sixty fisherman's sweaters for Peter Grimes and a hundred for Soldaat van Oranje.

entries.title: Rien Bekkers's costume dolls, Herenstraat
entries.reason: Okay; Location and Still there? unknown
entries.hook: A costume designer's window of metre-high dolls in 18th-century court dress, changed regularly.

entries.title: Singel 390, the globe melted down and hoisted back
entries.reason: Okay
entries.hook: A copper celestial globe between Apollo and Minerva, melted for copper in 1914 and remade in 2002.

entries.title: De Vier Heemskinderen, four knights on one horse
entries.reason: Okay
entries.hook: A 1671 baker's stone at the corner where two city extensions meet: the four sons of Aymon on one horse.

enrich.add: Look for: the classicist graveyard gate with weeping putti on the Prinsengracht side (pin approximate, check)

enrich.add: add access hours (walk 2023); do not use the strongroom legend
local voice: neighbour Fred Geukes Foppen named the 44; flowers every 11 May at 10.55

enrich.add: resolved by coordinator (L25); local voice quote from Zeven 100
local voice: oil tanks "tot grote ergernis van de buurt", blubber dumped on the quay
